## Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: As on 15 August, 2025, the area sown under Kharif crops is 1039.81 lakh ha as compared to 1002.41 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. About 94.8 percent of the normal area has been sown under the Kharif season crops. The status of sowing under Rice, Pulses, Coarse Cereals and Sugarcane is better than in the same period of last year.

## 2. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Maximum temperatures is likely to be above normal in many parts of Central India, Gujarat, Rajasthan, East Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and NE India.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01 -Aug 17 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 1% higher than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India:(-)18%; (ii) Northwest India: 13%; (iii) Central India: 4%; and South Peninsula: 6%.
- Fresh low pressure area over west central adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal, off north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts and its likely intensification into a depression during next 24 Hours.
- Heavy to very heavy rainfall over Goa, Maharashtra (including Mumbai), Gujarat State during next 7 days with Extremely heavy falls over Konkan (including Mumbai) & Goa, Ghat area of Madhya Maharashtra during 17th -19th , Gujarat Region and during 18th -20th ; Saurashtra on 19th & 20th August with peak activity on 19th & 20th August.
- Heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Odisha during next two days with isolated extremely heavy over coastal Andhra Pradesh during 17th - 18th , Odisha and Telangana on 18th August.
- Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall likely over the most parts of the country.
- A low pressure area is likely to form over northwest Bay of Bengal & Adjoining Bangladesh region around 24th August, 2025.

District-wise rainfall distribution of States is attached in Annexure I.

## 3. Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 7th August 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 135.28 billion cubic meter, which is 74.1% of total live storage capacity (182.496 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 107 percent of last year's storage and 124 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

- b) Groundwater Levels : About 43.1% of the total monitoring wells show depth to water level in the range of 0 to 5 m below ground level and 37.6% show depth to water level in the range of 5 to 10 m below ground level. About 19.2% of the total monitoring wells show water level deeper than 10 m below ground level. The groundwater level fluctuation analysis of Pre-monsoon 2025 with decadal mean of Pre-monsoon (2015-2024) indicates that 67.7% of analysed wells are showing rise and 33.0% are showing fall in water level. Remaining 0.3% stations analysed do not show any change in water level.

As per the Ground Water Drought Indices (GWDI), in pre-monsoon 2025, 90% of the analysed wells are in the normal category, while 10% of the analysed wells are in the drought category.

<!-- image -->

- c) Seeds and Fertilizers : For Kharif 2025, certified seed availability is 178.64 lakh quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
4. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Rice (Varieties: PR 114, PR 126 & PR 131) (Southern Rice Black Streaked Dwarf Virus (SRBSDV)) in Haryana and (Swarming Caterpillar) in Assam. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level.

- Rainfall is likely to be above normal over most part of Central India, West India, Odisha, Jharkhand, and many parts of NW India, Telangana, and Gangetic West Bengal. Below Normal over south Uttar Pradesh and many parts of NE India, Kerala, Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra Pradesh.

## 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

## Soil Moisture Observation

- Soil moisture as on 14 August 2025 was similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of M.P, central parts of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Haryana, Punjab, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Rayalseema region of A.P., Tamil Nadu and southern parts of Bihar.
- It was lower than average of past 9 years in Northern parts of Bihar, in parts of Assam, north eastern parts of U.P., Assam, Gujarat, in western and southern parts of Rajasthan, southern parts of Odisha, few western districts of MP and coastal districts of AP.
